nodes.name: Judah Touro
nodes.note: Judah Touro (1775–1854), New Orleans merchant. His bequest, reported as $50,000 or $60,000 (≈ $1.9–2.2 million today), left in trust with Moses Montefiore for Jerusalem's Jewish poor, paid for Mishkenot Sha'ananim (1860), the first Jewish quarter outside the Old City walls.

nodes.name: Mishkenot Sha'ananim (1860)
nodes.note: Almshouses built 1859–60 outside Jerusalem's walls with the Touro bequest, overseen by Moses Montefiore, who bought the land from Ahmad Agha Duzdar, a former governor of Jerusalem.

nodes.name: Sir Ellis Kadoorie
nodes.note: Sir Ellis Kadoorie (died Hong Kong, 1922), Baghdad-born Jewish merchant of the Kadoorie family. He left about £1,000,000 (≈ $90–100 million today) for schools in Palestine or Iraq; the British government, not the Jewish community, received it and built two agricultural schools, one Arab and one Jewish.

nodes.name: Kadoorie agricultural school, Tulkarm (1930)
nodes.note: The Arab Kadoorie school, opened 1930 at Tulkarm with an English principal; today Palestine Technical University – Kadoorie.

nodes.name: Kadoorie Agricultural School, Kfar Tavor (1933)
nodes.note: The Jewish Kadoorie school, foundations laid 1931 at Um Jabal by Kfar Tavor, opened 1933; designed, like the Tulkarm school, by Austen Harrison.

nodes.name: Kalonymus Ze'ev Wissotzky
nodes.note: Kalonymus Ze'ev Wissotzky (1824–1904), Moscow tea merchant (Wissotzky Tea) and a leader of Hovevei Zion. He left about 1 million rubles to philanthropy; his executors, including Ahad Ha'am, made a first contribution of 100,000 rubles to the Technion in Haifa.

nodes.name: Aaron Aaronsohn
nodes.note: Aaron Aaronsohn (1876–1919), agronomist of Zikhron Ya'akov. Raised American backing for an agricultural research station at Atlit (1909); founded and led NILI, the spy ring that worked for British forces against the Ottomans; his 1916 memorandum in London helped place a Jewish national home in British policy.

nodes.name: Atlit agricultural experiment station (1909)
nodes.note: Jewish Agricultural Experiment Station at Atlit, founded 1909 with money Aaronsohn raised in the United States; later the base of NILI.

nodes.name: Blackstone Memorial (1891)
nodes.note: Petition by William Blackstone to President Benjamin Harrison (1891), signed by 431 prominent Americans, among them John D. Rockefeller, J. P. Morgan, the future president William McKinley and Chief Justice Melville Fuller, asking that Palestine be given to the Jews.

nodes.name: John D. Rockefeller
nodes.note: John D. Rockefeller (1839–1937), founder of Standard Oil; a signatory of the Blackstone Memorial of 1891. No funding of the Zionist movement by him is in this record.

nodes.name: Benjamin Harrison
nodes.note: Benjamin Harrison, US President 1889–93; addressee of the Blackstone Memorial.

nodes.name: Bricha (1944–1948)
nodes.note: The organized flight of Jewish survivors from eastern Europe; about 100,000 left in the three months after the Kielce pogrom of 1946, and some 250,000 were moved into Austria, Germany and Italy by 1948, much of it toward Palestine through Aliyah Bet.

nodes.name: London arms appeal (1948)
nodes.note: In the Commons on 3 Feb 1948 an MP said a fund of £200,000 for 'arms for Jews in Palestine' had opened in Shoreditch, the first £100,000 in ten days; the Treasury said it had no power to stop the money being sent. The figures are the MP's, unverified.

nodes.name: Henry Morgenthau Jr.
nodes.note: Henry Morgenthau Jr. (1891–1967), US Treasury Secretary for twelve years under Roosevelt and Truman. In January 1947, after leaving office, he became general chairman of the United Jewish Appeal for its $170 million campaign, the appeal that funded the Jewish Agency through the United Palestine Appeal.

nodes.name: Ben Hecht
nodes.note: Ben Hecht (1894–1964), Hollywood screenwriter; with the Bergson group he raised money and recruits for the Irgun, wrote the 1946 play A Flag Is Born, and Irgun ships bore his name.
